ICYMI O/N 
 
MACRO:
 
US President Trump said in a Reuters interview he has no plans to fire Fed Chair Powell despite the Justice Department's criminal investigation, but it was "too early" to say what he would ultimately do. Trump said, "Right now, we're (in) a little bit of a holding pattern with him, and we're going to determine what to do. But I can't get into it. It’s too soon. Too early.” (RTRS)
 
The US imposed a 25% tariff on imports of certain advanced semiconductors from Nvidia (H200) and AMD (MI325X), a key step in an agreement blessed by President Trump allowing the companies to ship AI processors to China. The president is holding off for now on applying tariffs to a broader swath of foreign-made chips, instead he directed the admin to “pursue negotiation of agreements” on imports and to report back in 90 days, according to the proclamation he signed. (BBG)
 
China is working to set rules on how many advanced AI chips companies can buy from foreign makers like Nvidia, Nikkei Asia has learned, effectively allowing some sales by Nvidia instead of banning them outright. (Nikkei)
 
Trump said on Wednesday he had opted for now against imposing tariffs on rare earths, lithium and other critical minerals, and instead ordered his administration to seek supplies from international trading partners. (RTRS)
 
The cryptocurrency and banking industries are locked in a lobbying battle over digital tokens that yield annual payouts, a fight that threatens to derail legislation intended to bring crypto into mainstream finance. (WSJ)
 
Trump’s “unpredictable” policies have prompted bond giant Pimco to diversify away from US assets, as Wall Street frets over the long-term consequences of the president’s attacks on the Federal Reserve. Dan Ivascyn, CIO of Pimco, told the FT that the $2.2tn fund manager was “diversifying” its portfolios as it contends with the US president’s rapidly changing policies, which have caused flare-ups in market volatility. (FT)
 
Minneapolis officials called for calm Wednesday night as heated clashes erupted near the scene where a federal agent shot and injured a man after he allegedly assaulted the agent, one week after an immigration agent killed a woman in the city. (CNN)
 
The shipping market is being shaken up by Washington’s intervention in Venezuela, as the prospect of more oil being exported to the US boosts regional tanker rates to their highest level in almost two years. (BBG)
 
Japan's Nikkei share average fell back from a record high on Thursday, as the yen's rebound weighed on exporters and a red-hot rally in technology shares lost steam. (RTRS)
 
Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Thursday the government hopes to make progress in selecting projects for its U.S.-bound investment package if Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi meets with U.S. President Donald Trump in March. (RTRS)
 
Japan's main opposition Constitutional Democratic Party of Japan and Komeito have agreed to establish a new political party, their leaders said on Thursday, in an attempt to present a united front against ruling parties that they see as too right-leaning. (RTRS)
 
Hedge funds are ignoring yen intervention warnings and wagering in the currency option markets that it may fall toward 165 to a dollar before Japanese authorities step in. (BBG)
 
More than two-thirds of Japanese firms expect the economy to suffer from frayed ties with China, with nearly half reporting or anticipating a direct business impact, a Reuters survey showed on Thursday. (RTRS)
 
Japan's wholesale inflation slowed in the year to December on sliding fuel costs, data showed on Thursday, a sign falling crude oil prices were offering some relief to companies facing rising labour and other raw material costs. (RTRS)
 
The Bank of Japan will likely wait until July before raising its key interest rate again, economists surveyed by Reuters say, with more than 75% of them expecting it to climb to 1% or higher by September from the current three-decade high of just 0.75%. (RTRS)
 
Hedge funds including Dymon Asia Capital, Polymer Capital Management and Lighthouse Partners have hired business development specialists in Japan to find the next generation of star investors. (BBG)
 
China will cut interest rates on various structural monetary policy tools by 25 basis points and boost its re-lending programme for supporting tech innovation by 400 billion yuan ($57.37 billion) to 1.2 trillion yuan, the central bank said on Thursday. (RTRS)
 
The Shanghai Futures Exchange said on Thursday that it would adjust the trading price limit range to 11% and margins for hedging positions to 12% from the settlement on January 15th. The bourse also planned to limit the maximum daily open positions to 800 lots for some clients. (RTRS)
 
Chinese stocks edged lower on Thursday, as sentiment weakened after regulators took measures in the previous session to cool the market. (RTRS)
 
China’s surprise tightening of margin financing underscores mounting concern among regulators that speculative excess — especially in pockets of the technology sector — risks morphing into a destabilizing bubble if left unchecked. (BBG)
 
China's yuan climbed to a fresh 32-month high against the dollar on Thursday, underpinned by a stronger midpoint guidance fix, though it fell short of market expectations. (RTRS)
 
Chinese banks extended 910 billion yuan ($130.54 billion) in new loans in December, up from 390 billion yuan in November and beating expectations (800 billion yuan), according to Reuters calculations based on data from the People's Bank of China on Thursday. (RTRS)
 
China's foreign exchange deposits rose to $1.07 trillion at the end of last year, the central bank said on Thursday, hitting the highest since data became available in 2002. (RTRS)
 
More than 100 coal-fired power station generator units are set to start supplying electricity worldwide in 2026 as China continues to develop projects using the fossil fuel even as it installs huge amounts of wind and solar power. (FT)
 
China’s hog market is poised to remain under strain through the first half of 2026, with excess supply and sluggish demand keeping producers on the defensive, despite incremental policy steps aimed at easing competitive pressures in China’s livestock sector, according to Securities Times citing analysts. (Securities Times)
 
The Pound found some strength and BoE cut pricing reduced after Britain's economy grew more strongly than expected in November, boosted by the return to normal production at Jaguar Land Rover after a cyberattack which hit the carmaker and its suppliers. GDP +0.3% vs exp. +0.1% and prev. +0.1% in October. (BBG)
 
The architect of the UK’s regulatory response to the financial crisis has accused the Bank of England of making a mistake by cutting its estimate of how much capital the banking system needs. (FT)
 
London Mayor Sadiq Khan has said AI could usher in new era of mass unemployment. The mayor will announce free AI skills training for all Londoners and a taskforce to ensure AI is embedded in every industry. (Sky)
 
UK estate agents grew more optimistic in December as easing borrowing costs and an end to budget uncertainty lifted some of the gloom that hung over the housing market for much of last year. The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors said its gauge of expected home sales surged to 22, up from minus 4 the month before and the highest since October 2024. (BBG)
 
South Korea’s central bank held its base rate steady for a fifth consecutive meeting and removed a reference to potential rate-cuts from its policy statement, as weakness in the local currency limits room for further easing. (WSJ)
 
The South Korean won resumed its decline toward a 17‑year low on Thursday, testing officials’ resolve to stem the slide despite supportive remarks from US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. (BBG)
 
Singapore’s parliament has deemed Workers’ Party Secretary-General Pritam Singh “unsuitable” to serve as Leader of the Opposition following his conviction for lying to a parliamentary committee. (BBG)
 
GEOPOLITICAL:
 
US President Trump said to Reuters that Iranian opposition figure Reza Pahlavi "seems very nice, but I don't know how he'd play within his own country... And we really aren't up to that point yet." Trump said it is possible the government in Tehran could fall due to the protests but that in truth "any regime can fail... Whether or not it falls or not, it's going to be an interesting period of time," he said. (RTRS)
 
Iranian state media on Thursday reported that a 26-year-old man arrested during the protests in the city of Karaj would not be given the death sentence, after a rights group reported earlier this week that he was due to be executed on Wednesday. (RTRS)
 
Iran temporarily closed airspace around its capital Tehran to flights amid rising tensions with the US and nationwide protests in the country. (BBG)
 
Chinese officials have sought talks with Venezuelan and US officials to get assurances over its loans to the South American country, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)
 
The Senate voted to kill a war-powers resolution aimed at limiting President Trump’s authority in Venezuela, after the administration assured two pivotal GOP lawmakers that the U.S. has no plans to deploy ground troops or pursue a military occupation. (WSJ)
 
US President Trump wrote in a Truth Social post that after a call with Interim President of Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, "We are making tremendous progress, as we help Venezuela stabilize and recover. Many topics were discussed, including Oil, Minerals, Trade and, of course, National Security." (Truth)
 
Trump reiterated on Wednesday that the U.S. needs Greenland and that Denmark cannot be relied upon to protect the island, even as he said that "something will work out" with respect to the future governance of the Danish overseas territory. (RTRS)
 
Top officials from Denmark and Greenland said after a visit to the White House on Wednesday that they hadn’t persuaded President Trump to abandon his ambitions to annex Greenland. (WSJ)
 
Trump told Reuters that Ukraine - not Russia - is holding up a potential peace deal, rhetoric that stands in marked contrast to that of European allies, who have consistently argued Moscow has little interest in ending its war in Ukraine. (RTRS)
 
More U.S. arms sales to Taiwan are in the pipeline with four deals yet to be notified to Congress, a senior Taiwanese defence official said on Thursday, following the announcement of an $11 billion package last month, the largest ever for the island. (RTRS)
 
Japan and the Philippines signed a military logistics support agreement on Thursday, deepening their defense ties as they face rising tensions with China. (BBG)
 
EQUITIES:
 
Semiconductor stocks are leading tech strength premarket after TSMC said it expects capital spending to surge to as much as $56 billion in 2026, a stronger-than-anticipated projection that signals its confidence in the longevity of the global AI boom. (BBG)
 
ASML Holding NV shares soared to a record high, sending its market value beyond $500 billion, after Asian peer Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. gave a stronger-than-anticipated outlook for 2026. (BBG)
 
Intel and AMD are raising CPU prices amid shortages and rising costs, and with DRAM prices also surging, the PC market and makers could be hit. Both CPU makers are said to have nearly sold out all server processor capacity for the year, both for AI and cloud servers. (UDN via @dnystedt)
 
OpenAI's first AI chip, Titan, will launch by end-2026, media report. Co-developed with Broadcom, it will be made on TSMC’s 3nm mfg process. Titan II, the next-gen chip, will use TSMC’s A16 process. OpenAI has tapped Samsung’s 2nm Exynos chip for its AI earbuds, ‘Sweetpea’. (CTEE via @dnystedt)
 
Elon Musk’s xAI is disabling the ability for people to use its Grok AI chatbot to create sexualized images of real people, following widespread criticism that the company was allowing women and children to be victimized by the tool. (BBG)
 
California Attorney General Investigating xAI Over Grok’s Deepfakes. (WSJ)
 
Switzerland’s competition commission has begun a preliminary investigation into Microsoft Corp. over the licensing fees it charges clients in the country after receiving complaints over recent price increases. (BBG)
 
Paramount Skydance Corp. said board member Dennis Cinelli will become chief financial officer, appointing a permanent executive to the position as it continues to fight for control of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. (BBG)
 
Coinbase Global Inc. has pulled its support for the current version of the market-structure bill due for markup in the Senate Banking Committee on Thursday. (BBG)
 
Soho House shares rose after the company said it entered into a new funding commitment agreement — which will allow it to close a deal to go private — after its previous funding fell through. (WSJ)
 
SK Hynix plans to accelerate the opening of a new factory by three months and will also begin operating another new plant in February, a senior executive said, as surging memory demand pressures global supply. (RTRS)
 
Alibaba is rolling out a major update of its Qwen app, integrating the chatbot into its ecosystem and allowing it to carry out tasks on users’ behalf. With the update, users can ask Qwen to perform actions such as ordering milk tea and booking flights, rather than navigating different apps by themselves. Shares were lower on the session. (WSJ)
 
China Vanke has proposed further extending the grace period for a 2 billion yuan bond repayment that matured on December 15 to 90 trading days, a filing showed on Thursday. (RTRS)
 
The State Grid Corp. of China plans to boost spending to 4 trillion yuan ($574 billion) over the next five years, as the nation races to expand its power network to keep pace with rising electricity demand and build-out of renewables. (BBG)
 
China’s biggest securities firms are back on the offensive after taking a battering over the past few years. Investment banking divisions of major brokerages, including Citic Securities Co., Huatai Securities Co. and CSC Financial Co., have in recent months recruited dozens of junior and mid-level bankers, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)
 
China’s state-owned iron ore trader is checking on Jimblebar stockpiles held by some steel mills at Chinese ports, a sign that restrictions on the ore mined by BHP Group could be partially lifted. (BBG)
 
Cartier-owner Richemont said jewelry sales continued to drive revenue growth at the end of the year, offering fresh good news for a luxury-goods sector hoping to build momentum over the year ahead. (WSJ)
 
Rio Tinto and BHP Group have agreed to work together on some new projects at neighboring iron-ore mines in Australia that could help bolster their future production of the steel ingredient. (WSJ)
 
The UK housing marked continues to be blighted by lackluster demand as buyers struggle with elevated mortgage costs that have stretched affordability, according to Taylor Wimpey Plc. (BBG)
 
Asda hit by debt sell-off after Christmas sales slump. (FT)
 
The London Stock Exchange Group Plc has launched a new blockchain-friendly digital settlement service, as the bourse operator deepens its use of the technology underpinning cryptocurrencies. (BBG)
 
Illegal sports streaming is surging in the UK, fueled by sites that are largely funded by advertising from unlicensed gambling operators, as fans seek to dodge rising subscription costs on legitimate platforms. (BBG)

Too early.” (RTRS) The US imposed a 25% tariff on imports of certain advanced semiconductors from Nvidia (H200) and AMD (MI325X), a key step in an agreement blessed by President Trump allowing the companies to ship AI processors to China. (BBG) China is working to set rules on how many advanced AI chips companies can buy from foreign makers like Nvidia, Nikkei Asia has learned, effectively allowing some sales by Nvidia instead of banning them outright. (Nikkei) Trump said on Wednesday he had opted for now against imposing tariffs on rare earths, lithium and other critical minerals, and instead ordered his administration to seek supplies from international trading partners. (RTRS) The cryptocurrency and banking industries are locked in a lobbying battle over digital tokens that yield annual payouts, a fight that threatens to derail legislation intended to bring crypto into mainstream finance. (WSJ) Trump’s “unpredictable” policies have prompted bond giant Pimco to diversify away from US assets, as Wall Street frets over the long-term consequences of the president’s attacks on the Federal Reserve.
